meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class. Nobody called me first. Before you say anything else, I want to know who decided on that zero, and when.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
You didn't answer my question, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in? Then show me your version history.
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
I'm writing those times down: 11:52 and 11:58. What date, and turn the screen so I can read it myself. You still haven't told me who decided on that zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone called me, a straight answer on who decided it, and a look at that version history with its date. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to know who decided it, which is short of the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended well before her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing moved her position, though reading out exact edit times was the right kind of evidence, because it was specific and tied to Owen's own work.
What cost ground: You skipped her first question about who decided the zero and whether Owen was heard, which kept her focused on the school acting before asking.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your late-night edit times came close to that kind of night, though you gave no date; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open by owning in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called her, then give the date of those two edits and turn the screen so she can check the history herself.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
Write the email Owen should send me to apologize.
